questions: If there are multiple possible sets of K elements that include A_i, should we output the maximum GCD among those sets, the minimum GCD, or something else?
When K = 1, is the answer for each i simply A_i, or is there any special handling required?
Are the elements chosen for each i allowed to be any K elements from the entire sequence, or must they be contiguous or respect the original order?
Must the K chosen elements be distinct positions in the array, or can the same value at different indices be considered multiple times?
If N = K, does the answer for each i equal the GCD of the whole array, or is there any alternative interpretation?
Are there any constraints on the time or memory limits that could affect the choice of algorithm, or are they unspecified?
Should the output GCD values be printed as integers on separate lines without any extra spaces or formatting?
In case the GCD of a chosen set is 0 (e.g., if all chosen elements are 0, though A_i ≥ 1), how should that be handled, or is this situation impossible?
answers: For each i, the task is to find the maximum possible GCD among all selections of K elements that include A_i.
Yes, when K=1 the only choice is A_i itself, so the answer is A_i.
The order of the chosen K elements does not matter since GCD is order-independent; they need not be contiguous.
Positions are treated as distinct even if values repeat, so equal values at different indices count as separate elements.
Yes, when N=K the only choice is the whole array, so the answer is its GCD.
Not specified beyond what's given; assume standard algorithmic time/memory limits for this constraint size.
Each answer should be printed on its own line, as already stated in the Output section.
This case cannot occur since all A_i >= 1, so the GCD of a non-empty selection is always positive.
inline_prompts: You are given a sequence A = (A_1, A_2, \dots, A_N) of length N and a positive integer K (at most N). For each i = 1, 2, \dots, N, solve the following problem: When you choose K elements from A that include A_i, find the maximum possible GCD (greatest common divisor) of those chosen elements. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N K A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output Print N lines. The j-th line should contain the answer for i=j. Constraints - 1 \leq K \leq N \leq 1.2 \times 10^6 - 1 \leq A_i \leq 10^6 - All input values are integers.
